use_case_name: Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to reduce the redundancy of surveillance track reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the objective that the Primary Actor (C2 JU) aims to achieve by using PPLI data, which directly answers the 'goal' slot.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a track/point and another track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the goal of the use case: to associate related surveillance tracks and points using the J7.7 message.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU shall extrapolate the received target's position to the time of transmission.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly describes a specific objective and action ('shall extrapolate') that the primary actor (C² JU) must perform within the context of handling surveillance tracks obtained from other units, which contributes to the overall goal of associating related surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to associate a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point with an existing track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the objective of associating an ASW point with an existing track, which directly defines the 'goal' slot for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU has the responsibility to determine whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective (goal) of the primary actor (C2 JU) regarding track reporting and conflict detection.

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to resolve dual designations (determine if two tracks represent the same object) and initiate action to correlate them.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective of the C2 JU in this context: recognizing when two tracks are eligible for correlation and resolving the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state condition required before the C2 JU can proceed with specific reporting actions (assuming responsibility), which serves as a precondition for processing tracks under these rules.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate one track/point with any other point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a negative precondition or constraint on the system state regarding message usage before association can occur; specifically, correlation must not have been attempted via J7.2.

evidence_cards.content: After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C2 JUs capable of assuming R2 for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the required system state (Active status) and mandatory procedural steps (checks, correlation, registration) that must be completed before the C2 JU can begin transmitting track data, which is a prerequisite for any association use case.

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes specific temporal preconditions (time delays) that must elapse before the system is permitted to transmit tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the specific state condition (recognition of eligibility) required before the C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2, Correlation Rejection, shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a temporal precondition (cool-down period) that must hold before a new correlation request can be initiated after rejection.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines mandatory preconditions (track compatibility constraints) that must be satisfied before automatic acceptance of correlation can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have correlated local sensor data to assume R² of an Interface Unit (IU) and initiate reporting as a track or point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the specific system state (correlated local sensor data) required for the C2 JU to begin the process of handling/reporting an IU, which serves as the entry context for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: There is no interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation and the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate one track/point with any other point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a system state condition that must hold: the system does not use automatic correlation via J7.2, implying associations must be explicitly indicated (e.g., via J7.7) rather than assumed from correlated data.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a track/point and another track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the required mechanism for indicating association — this implies that before initiating the use case, the system must be configured or capable of transmitting J7.7 messages for association purposes.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a system state condition (presence of ID conflict) that must be evaluated and absent for automatic correlation to proceed; systems may inhibit this restriction via initialization parameter.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if the two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a precondition related to Mode II code mismatch with current local code that prevents automatic correlation unless inhibited by operator-selectable capability.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a system state condition (both tracks being locally derived real-time) that must not hold for automatic correlation to occur.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1; however, correlation is not inhibited if either track has Strength set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a threshold-based precondition on the Strength field value that blocks automatic correlation unless the value is 'No Statement'.

evidence_cards.content: A TN pair must be determined to be a dual designation before the C2 JU can initiate transmission of the J7.2 correlation message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the specific system state condition (dual designation determination) that must hold before the use case (associating tracks via J7.2 message) can begin.

evidence_cards.content: An association shall be terminated by the JU which had originated the association when it is determined that the association no longer exists.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a state condition regarding the lifecycle of an association (specifically termination) that must hold or be handled before re-associating tracks, ensuring data consistency.

evidence_cards.content: JUs should purge received data if data have not been updated after a specified time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a system state requirement where stale association data may need to be purged to ensure valid inputs for new associations.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a required system state condition — correlation of local sensor data by the C2 JU — that must hold before the use case of associating tracks/points can proceed under specific reporting contexts.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG if J2 messages are not received subsequent to integrating a PPLI report into its surveillance database and it still has no local data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a precondition boundary: absence of local data after integration negates reporting responsibility, implying that presence of local data or prior correlation is a necessary condition for initiating association actions.

evidence_cards.content: There is no interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation and the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate one track/point with any other point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a system state constraint (absence of automatic correlation) that serves as a precondition for the manual association use case, defining what must NOT happen automatically before the actor intervenes.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These restrictions define specific system state conditions that must be absent (i.e., no conflicts, no differing Mode II codes with local current status, not both locally derived real-time, no strength > 1) before automatic correlation can proceed, thus serving as preconditions for initiating association.

evidence_cards.content: The association of a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point with an existing track is initiated when further refined information concerning that point becomes available.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state (availability of further refined information) required to trigger the use case of associating points with tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the system state condition required before the C2 JU can recognize that two tracks are eligible for correlation — namely, that periodic comparisons have been performed and a dual designation has been identified. This is a prerequisite for initiating the association use case described in paragraph b.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action...
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly states the precondition: the C2 JU must first recognize that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation. This recognition triggers the initiation of action to resolve the dual designation, which aligns with the start boundary of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The system must be in a state where C2 JUs are receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specific message state is a required condition for the use case logic regarding correlation rejection and operator alerts to apply.

evidence_cards.content: The system must be in a state where C2 JUs are receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specific message state is a required condition for the automatic acceptance of requested correlation to occur, subject to restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall attempt to correlate received PPLI reports with data being received from local sensors.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific action (attempting correlation) that triggers the subsequent processing logic for associating tracks/points.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a track/point and another track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence specifies the exact action (transmitting a J7.7 message) that constitutes the trigger for the 'Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points' use case, distinguishing it from other messages like J7.2 which are explicitly forbidden for this purpose.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is the availability of further refined information concerning a subsurface fix or one of the other ASW points reported as specified in paragraph 4.4.5.2.3.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text explicitly identifies the event (availability of refined information) that initiates the process of associating a point with an existing track.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the trigger event (recognition of eligibility) and the initiating actor (C2 JU) for resolving dual designations, which is the specific context for track association/correlation in this document section.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for processing a correlation request occurs when the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This condition initiates the specific sequence of actions (checking for OCC and RV values) that defines the start of the use case scenario described on this page.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for handling a received J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs as contained in the transmission of the own unit J7.2 message sequence in progress.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This event starts the specific conflict resolution process described in paragraph i.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is the availability of PPLI data from J2 messages to be used by C2 JUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states the condition (availability of PPLI data) that initiates the integration and correlation process described in the section.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 message shall be used to indicate any association between a track/point and another track/point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the exact system action (transmitting J7.7) that constitutes the trigger event for the use case, as it is the mechanism by which the C2 JU initiates the association.

evidence_cards.content: The decision to report a DATUM shall be an operator function.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific user action (operator decision) that triggers the reporting of a track as a DATUM when contact is lost.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when C2 JU is handling a track/point and another track/point that are to be related through an association.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event or user action (handling tracks/points for association) that starts the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track except when that track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as was previously being used as the reference TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific event (ceasing to report a track) that triggers the transmission of a termination message, which serves as a trigger for the system to process track termination logic.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to report its own status is receiving a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message containing its own TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly identifies the event that starts the use case for the C2 JU reporting its own status.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a TN pair is determined to be a dual designation, the recognizing JU shall initiate transmission of the J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN selection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the event (determination of a TN pair as a dual designation) that triggers the initiating action (transmission of the J7.2 message) for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow step for the 'Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points' use case is sending the J7.7 Association (ACT = 0) Associate Data message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific system action (message transmission) required to successfully execute the association of tracks/points as described in the goal.

evidence_cards.content: Because Subsurface (Maritime) surveillance uses different information sources than Air, Surface, or Land surveillance, standard correlation procedures are not applied; instead, the operator performs manual correlation by using the J7.7 Track Association message whenever it is determined that two Track Numbers (TNs) are being used to report information for the same target.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action (using J7.7 message) and the actor (operator) required to associate related subsurface tracks in the main flow.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the primary actor's initiation step in the main flow of resolving track associations/dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the specific system interaction (message transmission) required to execute the association/correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a system-imposed delay constraint on re-attempting correlation after rejection, which is part of the main flow interaction sequence following a rejection event.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies actor action (operator alert) triggered by rejection in manual correlation context — part of the canonical success scenario’s exception handling within main flow.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies...
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the default successful path (automatic acceptance) upon receiving RV=3, forming the core of the main flow when no restrictions apply.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Post-acceptance stabilization rule that constrains subsequent system behavior — part of the completed main flow outcome.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU terminates an association when it is determined that the association no longer exists.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific action (termination) performed by the primary actor (JU) as part of managing associations, which constitutes a step in the main flow or a defined variant/exception path.

evidence_cards.content: JUs should purge received data if data have not been updated after a specified time interval.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a system maintenance action regarding association data, potentially part of the post-conditions or exception handling for stale data.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for the Association use case consists of a single step: C2 JU sends a J7.7 message with ACT = 0 to indicate an Associate Data message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This entry defines the specific message and action code (ACT=0) used for the primary 'Associate' function in the normal interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a primary action in the main flow when no existing track is correlated with incoming data — integration into surveillance database.

evidence_cards.content: If J2 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception or termination condition within the main flow — lack of follow-up messages leads to relinquishing reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a conditional step in the main flow where association is broken due to decorrelation criteria being met.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the next action after decorrelation — initiating a new track report, which is part of the canonical success scenario for handling unassociated points.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details specific field values required during the post-decorrelation reporting step — concrete constraint on output format in main flow.

evidence_cards.content: It is the function of the operator to perform manual correlation of Subsurface surveillance data, as automated correlation procedures for Air, Surface, or Land tracks are not applied to Subsurface tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for resolving dual designations involves the C2 JU recognizing two tracks eligible for correlation and initiating action (automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation. The recognizing JU then transmits a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks. The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This text describes the step-by-step normal interaction sequence between the primary actor (C2 JU) and the system (other IUs) for the specific use case of associating related tracks (resolving dual designations), including the trigger condition (recognition of eligibility) and the subsequent message transmission and acceptance steps.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response and timing constraint following a rejection event in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where the system retains the external PPLI track and drops its own local track based on TN comparison, achieving the association goal through a different decision logic than the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes two alternative successful paths: one where PPLI data replaces J3 data when TNs match, and another exception within that path where poor quality PPLI causes the system to retain the original surveillance track instead.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity (e.g., the Reference TN used for a reference/emergency point shall not be used for another entity type except in normal TN reuse).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific constraint on the association process regarding entity types, representing a variation or restriction in the flow when handling different surveillance entities.

evidence_cards.content: As an exception to the rule against changing Point Type/Amplification while retaining the same Reference TN, a Point Amplification value of 'No Statement' may be changed to a non-'No Statement' value and retain the same Reference TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides a specific legal alternative path for modifying point attributes during association that diverges from the general prohibition.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R² to another JU, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow for track termination where responsibility is transferred rather than simply dropped, altering the standard message transmission sequence.

evidence_cards.content: When a track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted upon cessation of reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a second exception/alternative path where the track status changes to Active IU, preventing the generation of a drop track report.

evidence_cards.content: Further refined information concerning a subsurface fix or one of the other ASW points reported as specified in paragraph 4.4.5.2.3 above may result in a Subsurface surveillance track which would then be reported with a new TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where refined point information leads to creation of a new track (with new TN) instead of associating with an existing track — diverging from the main flow’s association action.

evidence_cards.content: The reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point may be associated with an existing track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms the main flow option; included here to contrast with the alternative (new TN) and establish that both are valid outcomes under the same trigger condition.

evidence_cards.content: When a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix shall be used for the new AOP.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a variant path in track association where an existing fix's Track Number (TN) is reused instead of assigning a new one, which constitutes an alternative flow to the standard rule of assigning a new TN for AOPs resulting from multiple sources.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action either automatically or manually to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative path where manual intervention is used instead of automatic processing to resolve track associations, diverging from the standard automated flow.

evidence_cards.content: The originating JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation; when the RV field is set to value 1 it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.

evidence_cards.content: J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request is transmitted by any JU and initiated by operator action, serving as an alternative mechanism to request updated IFF/SIF data when needed.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.4 message can be used to report (Report/Request TN field set to value 0) or request (Report/Request TN field set to value 1) Track Numbers (TNs) individually, collectively, or in any combination.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.4 report message may be transmitted by any JU in response to a J7.4 request message or as the result of operator action.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may originate, by operator action only, the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message for the clearing of one or more modes on the specified track.

evidence_cards.content: All JUs, upon receipt of the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, shall automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status (except that acceptance or rejection of a received J7.5 (ACT=0) Mode IV Clear message may be automatic or by operator determination).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes system response to J7.5 (ACT=0) — sets track to No Data status, which is a legal alternative path that terminates association intent and replaces it with data-clearing behavior.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R², upon receiving or initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message that results in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track, shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies consequence of J7.5 (ACT=0) initiation/receipt: halts transmission of IFF/SIF-containing J3 messages, altering normal surveillance reporting flow — valid alternative path affecting post-association data handling.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may change a local mode to a No Data status without transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides another alternative flow: local-only mode-to-No-Data transition without network messaging, bypassing J7.5 entirely — still achieves same end state (No Data) but via non-networked path.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur as a result of an operator action wherein the update request is transmitted in a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request message.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.5 (ACT = 3) message is used to exchange codes that have special meaning for implementing JUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes another variant of J7.5 message (ACT=3) that could represent an alternative flow for exchanging specially coded association-related data.

evidence_cards.content: J7.7 Association (ACT = 1) Terminate Association message provides an alternative path to end an association.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the system successfully resolves a conflict between tracks from different JUs by retaining the external PPLI data and dropping the local surveillance track, diverging from the standard manual association or automatic acceptance flows.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative path for handling identical Track Numbers from different sources, including a specific sub-condition (Quality = 0) that reverses the default behavior, representing a complex variant of the main association logic.

evidence_cards.content: If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a legal alternative path that diverges from the main flow after conflict resolution steps (c) or (d), specifying an additional required test before successful association can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception condition where the association fails due to timeout, leading to cancellation — not a successful alternative path, but critical context for understanding valid vs invalid flows.

evidence_cards.content: Differences in position, velocity, or altitude/elevation recognized by a JU are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message; however, these differences may cause a JU to assume that one TN represents two different tracks or different TNs are being used to report the same track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative handling path for surveillance data differences where standard conflict resolution is bypassed, resulting in potential duplicate track assumptions rather than association messages.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R², except when the JU relinquishes R² to another JU or when the track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies exception conditions under which the standard termination message is suppressed, representing a valid alternative flow for track data management.

evidence_cards.content: If contact is regained after a DATUM has been reported, the C2 JU reports a J3.4 message with DRT set to value 0, 1, or 2 using the same Track Number (TN) as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where the system recovers from the 'contact lost' state (which triggers the main flow of reporting a DATUM) by regaining contact, requiring a specific message update to transition back to active tracking.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative path involving operator intervention (voice coordination) triggered by a rejection event in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: An association shall be terminated by the JU which had originated the association when it is determined that the association no longer exists.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a valid alternative path for terminating an association after it has been established, diverging from the main flow of creating/maintaining the association.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines explicit exception conditions that prevent manual correlation (association) from occurring, which constitutes an exception flow for the 'Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points' use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines explicit exception conditions under which automatic correlation is inhibited for C2 JU during track association, directly constraining the exception_flow of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies an exception to the Strength-based inhibition rule — specifically, when Strength is 'No Statement', correlation is not blocked, which refines the exception handling logic.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where the C2 JU must terminate its responsibility (R²) for a track due to receiving superior data from another unit, interrupting the normal association flow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a timeout-based exception condition that triggers a change in track reporting responsibility (assumption of R²).

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) Environment/Category and ID are different from the local Environment/Category and ID, the Environment/Category conflict shall be processed and resolved prior to the resolution of the ID conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception handling path for conflicting surveillance data that must be resolved before proceeding with normal track association processing.

evidence_cards.content: If an Environment/Category conflict is detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict need occur.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a terminal condition in the exception flow where detection of one type of conflict prevents further processing of another type.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception flow where the receiving unit fails to meet implementation requirements for the specific data change, resulting in a forced termination of reporting and transmission of a cancel message instead of accepting the association.

evidence_cards.content: Units receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 2) Change Data Order message containing an ID of Pending shall not accept that order.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception condition where the content of the received message (ID of Pending) causes the system to reject the operation rather than proceeding with the standard acceptance logic.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall not accept the requested correlation when local or remote data indicates: (1) There is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g; (2) The Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate once subjected to the decorrelation criteria; (3) There is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0 (reverse correlation transmitted if new Dropped TN has no constraint, otherwise rejected); (4) There is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific exception conditions under which the C2 JU must reject an automatic correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system response mechanism for reporting a rejected correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly states a terminal exception condition where correlation is impossible due to constraints on both tracks.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception conditions that override the default acceptance behavior for manually initiated correlations.

evidence_cards.content: A code of all zeroes (00 or 0000) is illegal for use as an assigned operational IFF/SIF Mode I, II, or III code. Any IFF/SIF Mode I, II, or III Code field set to all zeroes indicates that the reporting unit has no data.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 Association (ACT = 1) Terminate Association message is defined as a distinct message type from the Associate Data message (ACT = 0).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific system action for terminating an association, which serves as the response mechanism in an exception flow where an existing association must be dissolved due to error or conflict before a new one can be established.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point, line, or area shall not be required to purge the point, line, or area; however, if it does not purge, it shall assume R² for that entity to ensure it remains active on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where receipt of a termination/deactivation message (J7.0 ACT=0) does not force immediate purging but instead triggers a responsibility assumption (R²) to maintain interface activity — relevant as an alternative handling path when association context involves such messages.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU fails to receive the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and further updates are not received, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN. If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.

evidence_cards.content: If contact is regained after a DATUM report, a J3.4 message with DRT set to value 0, 1 or 2 shall be reported with the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.7 message is totally independent of the J6.0, J10.6, J7.2, and J10.2 messages and may be transmitted concurrently with those messages.

evidence_cards.content: An association shall be terminated by the JU which had originated the association when it is determined that the association no longer exists.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity; i.e., the Reference TN used to identify a particular reference or emergency point shall not be used for any other type of entity reported on the interface except in the normal course of TN reuse.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change the Point Type and/or Point Amplification value of a reference point while retaining the same Reference TN, with one specific exception allowing a Point Amplification value of 'No Statement' to be changed to a non-'No Statement' value while retaining the same Reference TN.

evidence_cards.content: Each message contains the special rules required for the transmission and reception of that message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the successful completion implies adherence to specific transmission/reception rules defined for the J7.7 message.

evidence_cards.content: The association between a track/point and another track/point is indicated by the use of the J7.7 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the successful end state (postcondition) of the use case: the indication of association via the specific message required in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The association between the related track/point and another track/point is indicated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the successful end state of the use case: the system has successfully associated a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point with an existing track, fulfilling the goal of indicating an association between tracks/points.

evidence_cards.content: The association between the related track/point and another track/point is indicated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim defines the success boundary for the use case; the postcondition is the state where the association has been successfully indicated via the J7.7 message.

evidence_cards.content: After successful association, the system indicates an association between a track/point and another track/point via transmission of a J7.7 message with ACT = 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition state — that an association has been indicated — which is the success boundary for the use case. The J7.7 (ACT=0) message is the mechanism by which this state is achieved and confirmed on the interface.

evidence_cards.content: EW association shall be reported using the J7.7 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Directly specifies the mechanism (J7.7 message) used to report an association between EW AOPs and surveillance tracks, which constitutes the observable system state change after successful completion of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.2 message may be used to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that while J7.2 can indicate correlation for EW AOPs, it is explicitly prohibited for correlating EW LOBs and fixes — reinforcing that J7.7 is the required channel for reporting associations involving those data types, thus defining the postcondition boundary.

evidence_cards.content: The association between a track/point and another track/point is terminated by the JU which originated it when determined that the association no longer exists.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific system state (termination of association) that results from the lifecycle management of the association created in this use case, serving as the end-state or post-condition for the association's validity period.

evidence_cards.content: JUs purge received association data if data have not been updated after a specified time interval.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a cleanup behavior (purging data) that occurs as a consequence of the association process, contributing to the final system state regarding stored data.
